questions.q: What does join kind=leftouter correspond to from Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 55?
options: The same "left" join — every left-side row kept, matched or not, with unmatched right-side columns coming back as null
An inner join, keeping only matched rows
A completely different join concept unique to KQL
A join that only works on streaming data, never static tables
questions.explain: KQL supports the same core join kinds, just with a slightly different default than SQL/PySpark's usual inner join.

questions.q: What do $left. and $right. do in a KQL join?
options: Disambiguate a column name that exists on both sides of the join
Specify which table is the streaming source
Convert the join into a leftouter join automatically
They have no functional purpose in KQL
questions.explain: This solves the exact same problem Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 55 solved with trips.VendorID vs. zones.VendorID.

questions.q: How does enriching RawTripEvents with a Zones join compare to the previous course's material?
options: It's genuinely the same enrichment pattern — turning a bare PULocationID into a readable zone name — just against a live stream instead of a static Delta table
There's no comparable pattern in the previous course
KQL joins cannot enrich streaming data at all
This only works with Warehouse tables, never KQL Database tables
questions.explain: The underlying join concept transfers directly, just applied to a different kind of source table.

questions.q: Why is joining a stream against a small, static lookup table simpler than joining two large, fast-moving streams?
options: Joining two streams requires deciding how long to wait for a late-arriving match before giving up — a complication a static-table join never faces
Static lookup tables cannot be used in KQL joins at all
There's no real difference in complexity between the two scenarios
Stream-to-stream joins are actually always faster
questions.explain: This is exactly why Lesson 33's watermarks exist — to handle that specific complication.

questions.q: What is KQL's default join kind, and how does it differ from SQL/PySpark's usual default?
options: innerunique — differing slightly from SQL/PySpark's usual inner-join default
leftouter, identical to PySpark's default
fullouter, unlike any common SQL default
KQL has no default join kind at all
questions.explain: KQL supports the same core kinds as other join languages, just with its own particular default behavior.
